headline: Central bankers meeting in Bangkok say the AI investment boom is pushing up the cost of borrowing and may keep interest rates higher.
score_reason: Named central bank leaders on record at a major meeting; important for rates but a general outlook rather than a new decision.
importance_line: Borrowers, including governments with large debts such as France, face higher costs first, then companies financing AI projects, but Lesetja Kganyago, governor of South Africa's central bank, says nobody knows how much higher the neutral interest rate, known as R-star, now is.
summary: Reuters reports that central bankers at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank meetings in Bangkok see AI spending on chips, data centres and power grids as a global race for money that raises borrowing costs before AI's productivity gains arrive. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh called the boom "a shock" that hits demand before supply, European Central Bank policymaker Martins Kazaks said there is "a global fight for money", and Bank of England chief economist Huw Pill said rates may on average be "that little bit higher".
notes: Reuters text read on the Devdiscourse syndicated copy; reuters.com link kept as the original.
